what_it_does: Quantum computers need to control individual quantum bits (qubits) with extraordinary precision using tiny voltage pulses, and today's approach requires long cables from room-temperature electronics down to the quantum chip sitting in a super-cooled freezer at 60 millidegrees above absolute zero. Those cables introduce electrical noise that ruins quantum operations. This paper puts the control electronics—specifically two precision voltage-controlled potentiometers (DACs—digital-to-analog converters) with 18-bit resolution—directly on the quantum chip itself, operating at cryogenic temperatures. The 18-bit precision means voltage control to within 4.6 microvolts, with noise so low (4.1 nanovolts per root hertz) that it enables reliable quantum gate control without the noise penalty of long cables.
